question: How the land border meshes of map/cache/all_quads.bin (pieces 3 and 4 of a tile's record) and map/cache/border_adj.bin are made from the map files. Checked byte for byte: every tile of TFH (1,774) and BlackICE (1,787) rebuilt from the map files agrees whole, and border_adj.bin of both.

addresses.name: QuadBuild_EdgeVertices
addresses.revises: The record had read only the stores and had no signature. Now the whole function: a quad or triangle for each pixel entry, the two streams, the slot rule, the junction lists of border_adj.bin. Signature given; confidence raised to confirmed.
addresses.signature: void __stdcall QuadBuild_EdgeVertices(WaterObject* mgr, void* pixelIndices, int* pixelIndexCount, void* provinceGroups, void* vertexCache, int* vertexCount, void* scratch, int* borderIndexCount, int* borderVertexCount)
addresses.comment: **One province's pixels into the tile's border quads, and the province's junction list.** Called once per province of the tile by the per-tile builder 0x4727B0 (call at 0x873069, one caller; a sea province's scratch record has no entries, so only land provinces do anything). `scratch` is the 0x6C-byte per-province record 0x456DF0 filled: +0 absolute pixels (int x, y; a diagonal pixel twice), +0x10 the pixels local to the province's centre (float), +0x30/+0x34 the centre less the tile's middle (float), +0x38 the id, +0x3C the pixel's type 0..4, +0x5C the offset to the id the entry stands for: (0,0), or (+-1,0) on a diagonal's second entry. For each entry: `own` = raster(x, y), `id` = raster(x + dx, y + dy), 0 outside the raster. **The eight neighbours in order NW, N, NE, W, E, SW, S, SE** (y grows north; slots 0..7 of the stack array). `flag` (is on a border) and `sel` (which neighbour): for own not in the sea set CMap +0x21F8, a neighbour that differs, is not sea and is not 0 sets flag, and sel takes it if sel was unset or the slot is N, W, E or S - so the last orthogonal one in that order wins, else the first diagonal. (The other arm, own in the sea set, cannot run here; it wants the neighbour in the sea set.) **Junction**: flag and any of the four corner pairs (N,W), (S,W), (N,E), (S,E) whose two ids both differ from own, differ from each other and are both not sea. A junction looks for (x, y) on mgr +0x42B4[own] and pushes it if absent - **that list is border_adj.bin**, in the order the pixels are walked; log 'To many corners in province' once it holds 8 or more, no cap on the push. **Slot**: junction = adjacency count (template +0x90, 0x14 a record) + min(index on the list, 7); otherwise the index of sel in the adjacency list, or -1 if it is not on it (a neighbour only by a diagonal). n = own x 14 + slot; **u = n & 0x1FF, v = n >> 9**. When flag is set a quad goes into g_pTempBorderIndices/Vertices at the border vertex count: indices base, +1, +2, +2, +3, +0 and four 0x18-byte records. Record: float x, float z, word u, word v, D3DCOLOR = (bitmap byte 3 x 8) << 24 | (id & 0xFF) << 16 | (id >> 8) << 8 | (bitmap byte 0 x 8), float uv-corner-u, float uv-corner-v; the bitmap is the CBorderManager's +0x3C at (x, y) - own's pixel, not the id's; so **a diagonal's second half carries the neighbour's id in its colour and own's slot**. Corners A (x-0.5, y-0.5, 0, 1), B (x-0.5, y+0.5, 0, 0), C (x+0.5, y+0.5, 1, 0), D (x+0.5, y-0.5, 1, 1) with x, y local to the tile's middle: by the entry's type 0 = A B C D (the whole pixel), 1 = A B D D, 2 = A C D D, 3 = A B C C, 4 = B C D D. **The same pixel entries also write the 12-byte stream** (`vertexCache` = g_pProvinceVertexMemCache, 12 bytes a vertex: float x, float z, words id & 0xFF and id >> 8, all pixels and not only the border's, indices to `pixelIndices`): nothing reads that buffer or the index vector, so it is dead (3 references to the global in the image: alloc, free, this caller) and +0x42C4 (a u16 vector of the entries' vertex numbers, only cleared by CProvinceManager_LoadQuads, 0x45A41A) likewise found no reader. It also keeps +0x4198[60] of the distinct province ids in the tile and +0x4190/+0x4194 the per-province index lists for the tile's +0x10 meshes (not read here). `ret 0x24`. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapcache.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Read whole from the decompilation with the corner and type sequence checked against the listing at 0x875A86..0x877564. A Python implementation of this rule from provinces.bmp, definition.csv and default.map (with the shipped border_bitmap.bin, map.bin and adjacencies.bin as inputs) gives every tile's border indices and vertices and border_adj.bin byte for byte on TFH (1,774 of 1,774 tiles) and BlackICE (1,787 of 1,787). Would be shown wrong by a tile of a map whose border mesh differs from the rule; the arms not exercised (own in the sea set, a slot of -1 reaching the file more than TFH's two quads) are named in the write-up. The record's name is kept, though the function does far more than edges.

addresses.name: TempBorderVertices_Weld
addresses.revises: Comment rewritten from the read (the drop rule, its dead second arm, the first-occurrence order) and confidence raised to confirmed.
addresses.comment: **Welds a tile's border records, in place**: g_pTempBorderVertices (0x18 bytes each) with g_pIndexLookup as the remap and g_pTempBorderIndices as the 16-bit triangle list, from the per-tile builder 0x4727B0 at 0x873480 where the tile has any border index. (1) Every remap -1, and -2 for a record whose colour byte B (+0xC, border bitmap byte 0 x 8) is 0 and whose byte A (+0xF, bitmap byte 3 x 8) is 0; **the second arm of the test, byte A == 0x16 with R (+0xE, id & 0xFF) == 0, cannot be true** - A is a multiple of 8 - so it is dead. (2) Walking i ascending, where remap[i] is -1: copy the record to the next free slot of g_pTempVertices, remap[i] = that slot, and every later record equal to it in x, z, u, v, colour and both uv corners gets that slot too. So the vertices come out in first-occurrence order and only duplicates within one pixel merge (a type-1..4 entry's doubled corner). (3) The compact copy goes back into g_pTempBorderVertices. (4) Triangle by triangle, the remapped indices are kept unless two of them are equal - the collapsed triangle of a doubled corner, or a dropped quad (all its indices -2). Order of the triangles unchanged. Writes the new counts through both pointers and adds what it removed to the counters at 0x1A85660/0x1A85664. `ret` (cdecl). The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapcache.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, decompilation and the opening listing (0x872560..0x8725C1; the 0x16 compare at 0x8725A7 against the byte at +0xF). Reproduces the vertices and indices of all tiles of TFH and BlackICE byte for byte. Would be shown wrong by a kept record equal to a later dropped one (impossible, the colour is part of the equality) or by any tile whose welded quad differed.

addresses.name: QuadBuild_AddPixelEntries
addresses.signature: void __stdcall QuadBuild_AddPixelEntries(void* zeros@EDX, WaterObject* mgr@stack:4, void* localPixels@stack:8, void* absolutePixels@stack:0xC, void* zeros2@stack:0x10, void* cutTypes@stack:0x14, void* offsets@stack:0x18, int px@stack:0x1C, int py@stack:0x20, int originX@stack:0x24, int originY@stack:0x28)
addresses.comment: **Adds one pixel to a tile's 0x6C-byte per-province record**, once or twice. px, py are the pixel from the template's +0x6C list, local to the province's centre (originX/Y = the template's +0x2C/+0x30); absolute = the two added. Pushes: 0 to EDX's int vector (+0x4C); (float px, float py) to localPixels (+0x10); the absolute pair to absolutePixels (+0); 0 to zeros2 (+0x20); (0, 0) to offsets (+0x5C); and to cutTypes (+0x3C) a type read from map.bin's raster at the absolute pixel, tested in this order: bit 2 -> 4, bit 8 -> 3, bit 4 -> 2, bit 1 -> 1, otherwise 0. **Where that type is not 0 the pixel goes on again**, as the second half of a diagonal: the float and absolute pixels a second time and to cutTypes bit 2 -> 1, bit 4 -> 3, bit 8 -> 2, bit 1 -> 4, with offsets (-1, 0) for bits 2 and 4 and (1, 0) for bits 8 and 1 - the side the id of that half is read from. (`m` 16, 32 and 48 alone give type 0 and one entry.) Two callers: the per-tile builder 0x4727B0 (0x872B01) and Quad_FillEntriesFromTileProvinces (0x8570DB). `ret 0x28`. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapcache.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Read whole in the listing, 0x856DF0..0x856F99. The types' mapping and the offsets are in every border quad of TFH and BlackICE, reproduced byte for byte. Would be shown wrong by a diagonal pixel whose quad's vertex order did not follow these types.

struct_fields.name: sea_starts_head
struct_fields.comment: Head of a linked list of province ids, each node {id, ?, next at +8}. default.map's `sea_starts`: CMap::LoadKey's `sea_starts` case parses the integer list into it (section D). CMap::LoadMapFiles turns it into the byte array at +0x21F8 (VA 0x489C20), and taking that set as sea_starts reproduces the land border meshes of two maps byte for byte. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapcache.md, section B.
struct_fields.evidence: VA 0x489C0A..0x489C2F walks the list and writes 1 per id; the reading as sea_starts is the LoadKey case, and the byte-for-byte result agrees. Would be shown wrong by a parser storing sea_starts elsewhere.

struct_fields.name: is_sea_by_id
struct_fields.comment: A byte per province id (province_count bytes, freed and zeroed at the head of CMap::LoadMapFiles), 1 for each id on the list at +0x21E8 - *inferred* default.map's `sea_starts`. Read by QuadBuild_EdgeVertices (0x4754D0) for its neighbour test and by MapBinCache_Build. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapcache.md, section B.
struct_fields.evidence: VA 0x489BD3..0x489C2F: operator new of province_count bytes, memset 0, 1 for each listed id. Reproduces the land border meshes of two maps byte for byte.

struct_fields.name: province_mesh_index_lists
struct_fields.comment: A vector of 16-byte vectors of 16-bit indices, one for each slot of +0x4198: QuadBuild_EdgeVertices appends six indices a pixel entry to the slot of the entry's province; the per-tile builder copies them into the tile's +0x10 meshes (0x873416). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapcache.md, section B.
struct_fields.evidence: QuadBuild_EdgeVertices at 0x8761xx and the copy at 0x873416. Not read further, in particular not the draw of the tile's +0x10 meshes.

struct_fields.name: province_mesh_index_counts
struct_fields.comment: How many indices each slot of +0x4190 holds. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapcache.md, section B.
struct_fields.evidence: QuadBuild_EdgeVertices' increments (0x4761xx); the builder reads it back at 0x873416.

struct_fields.name: province_mesh_ids
struct_fields.comment: The 60 slots' province ids for the tile being built, 0 where free: QuadBuild_EdgeVertices finds the entry's id or takes the first free slot. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapcache.md, section B.
struct_fields.evidence: The search and the store in QuadBuild_EdgeVertices (0x4754D0's head). 60 entries by the size of the walk, and the field runs up to +0x4288 where the record's next field stands.

struct_fields.name: border_edge_vertex_numbers
struct_fields.comment: Begin of a std::vector<uint16_t> (end +0x42C8, capacity +0x42CC): QuadBuild_EdgeVertices pushes the 12-byte stream's vertex number of border pixels' west and east corners and of a diagonal's halves, on a rebuild only. Cleared by CProvinceManager_LoadQuads (0x45A41A); **no reader found** (fieldchain finds the constructor, the release, LoadQuads' clear and, by the pushes through 0x449480, this function). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapcache.md, section B.
struct_fields.evidence: fieldchain.py --field 0x42C4 and the pushes in QuadBuild_EdgeVertices (0x476E.., the 'local_42 / local_41' branches). A negative with its positive control being the four sites it did find; would be shown wrong by a read through a pointer fieldchain does not follow.
